current.text: His assists and usage are lower when James Harden plays. With Harden he averaged about 5 assists per 36 minutes, against about 6.1 without him, and his usage was 30% instead of 32%. Harden is now with Cleveland for a full season.
Much of his strong 2025-26 line came while Darius Garland was out or limited and Max Strus was out, so he carried most of the load alone.
Cleveland added Peyton Watson. The projected starters are Harden, Mitchell, Watson, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, and Watson will also take touches.
He is expected to lose 20 to 25% of his assists with Harden there. One projection has him at just under 30% usage and 33 minutes.
His two-point percentage was the best of his career last season, and the experts expect it to come down. They also doubt he keeps his 1.5 steals. They do not expect him to repeat last season's level.
The second unit has no clear point guard, so Harden and Mitchell may stagger. A hard stagger would protect Mitchell's value. If they share most of their minutes, his value drops.

The experts agree he is not a first-round pick. They call Yahoo rank 13 too high and ESPN's top-10 rank far too high. One expert calls a rank of about 14 reasonable but would put him a bit lower. He also says taking him in round 1 will not sink a draft.
One expert would take Jamal Murray and Austin Reaves ahead of him. Another is lower on him than his draft cost.
In an auction mock draft he went for 31 USD.
The expert calls 31 USD about the right price for him.
One expert has concerns about his minutes and his health.
He has no current injury and was fairly healthy last season.
He has signed a contract extension with Cleveland.
Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league.
With a March 28 end, Cleveland plays 4, 3 and then 2 games in the fantasy playoffs. That means only two games in the finals week starting March 22.
Cleveland is projected to win about 51 to 53 games.

durable.text: He has had persistent knee problems.
He is 30 and has carried a heavy load over the last couple of years.
He was ranked about 30 to 40 for most of his career. Last season was the only time he played at a top-10 level.
Two-point percentage has always been his weak spot. His FG%, rebounds and blocks are not strong categories.
Points are a league outlier strength. Threes, steals, FT% and assists are also clearly above the top 250 pool.
Turnovers are his weakest category and are high for a guard.

note: Every expert says he is not a first-round pick, and the market prices him like one: Yahoo 44 USD (average cost 45.4), ESPN 59 USD. In our league he went for 40 USD last season, while an expert mock auction had him at 31 USD and called that fair. Aim for the low to mid 30s and let others pay 45 or more. He adds points, threes, steals and FT% and costs you turnovers, so he fits punt TO builds best. A two-game finals week hurts him. Early in the season, check how much he plays alongside Harden, whether his assists hold near 5 or more, and whether his steals and two-point shooting come down.
